seoTitle: Free AWS IAM Policy Builder from Plain Lines
metaDescription: Compose an AWS IAM policy JSON from simple lines of Effect, actions, resources and an optional condition. Free and runs in your browser.
intro: Write each statement as a line of effect, actions, resources and an optional condition, and get a valid IAM policy document in JSON.
why:
Writing IAM JSON by hand means juggling Statement arrays, single values versus lists, and nested Condition blocks, where one missing bracket produces an opaque error in the console. A compact line format makes the intent easier to see, and the JSON can be generated from it.

Here each line is one statement: Allow or Deny, comma-separated actions, comma-separated resource ARNs and, if you want, a condition such as StringEquals aws:RequestedRegion=eu-west-1. The tool checks the shape of each action and the effect, numbers the statement IDs and sets the 2012-10-17 version. It does not know which actions exist, so run the result through the IAM Policy Linter and the AWS policy simulator.
howTo: Write one statement per line: Effect | actions | resources | optional condition.
Add a principal only if you need a resource policy such as a bucket policy.
Copy the JSON into IAM, then lint it and test it in the policy simulator.

faq.q: What does the condition format look like?
faq.a: Use Operator key=value, for example StringEquals aws:RequestedRegion=eu-west-1. Several values can be separated with commas. Only one condition per statement is supported.

faq.q: When should I fill in the principal field?
faq.a: For resource-based policies such as S3 bucket policies. Leave it blank for identity policies attached to a user, group or role. Use a star for any principal, with care.

faq.q: Does it check that actions really exist?
faq.a: No. It checks the service:Action pattern and allows wildcards, but it has no list of AWS actions. A misspelt action will pass, so test in the policy simulator.
